subject: general
question: Which state notified the Tsarap Chu Conservation Reserve under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 to protect high-altitude biodiversity in 2025?

options.text: Sikkim for Himalayan red panda conservation purposes
Himachal Pradesh to secure snow leopard habitats
Uttarakhand to protect alpine medicinal plant species
Arunachal Pradesh to conserve high-altitude wetlands

solution: The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh to secure snow leopard habitats**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Himachal Pradesh** notified the **Tsarap Chu Conservation Reserve** under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** to safeguard high-altitude biodiversity, including habitats of the elusive **snow leopard**. • The Tsarap Chu Conservation Reserve is located in the **Lahaul-Spiti region**, which is renowned for its extreme altitude and ecological diversity. • Efforts to protect snow leopard habitats align with India's participation in the **Global Snow Leopard and Ecosystem Protection Program (GSLEP)**, an international initiative aimed at conserving snow leopards and their ecosystems. • The reserve plays a critical role in protecting endangered species, such as the **snow leopard**, and conserving fragile high-altitude ecosystems. • This initiative is part of a broader strategy by Himachal Pradesh to enhance wildlife conservation in the state and promote eco-tourism.
